title: Isaiah Chapter 42 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 42 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 42 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 42.

questions.question: Who is described as God’s servant in Isaiah 42:1?
options: Mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth
The kings of Israel
The prophets
The priests
questions.correctAnswer: Mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:1 calls the servant 'mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth,' indicating God’s chosen servant.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 42:2, how will the servant not act?
options: He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street
He shall shout loudly in the streets
He shall perform miracles publicly
He shall lead armies into battle
questions.correctAnswer: He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:2 states the servant 'shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street,' emphasizing his quiet nature.

questions.question: What will the servant not break, according to Isaiah 42:3?
options: A bruised reed
The law
The tables of stone
The covenant
questions.correctAnswer: A bruised reed
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:3 says, 'A bruised reed shall he not break,' showing the servant’s gentleness.

questions.question: Until when shall the servant not fail nor be discouraged, according to Isaiah 42:4?
options: Till he have set judgment in the earth
Till he conquers all enemies
Till he builds a temple
Till he gathers Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Till he have set judgment in the earth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:4 states the servant 'shall not fail nor be discouraged, till he have set judgment in the earth.'

questions.question: Who is credited with creating the heavens and the earth in Isaiah 42:5?
options: God the LORD
Moses
Isaiah
The angels
questions.correctAnswer: God the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:5 says, 'Thus saith God the LORD, he that created the heavens, and stretched them out; he that spread forth the earth.'

questions.question: What has the LORD put upon his servant, according to Isaiah 42:1?
options: His spirit
His sword
His crown
His name
questions.correctAnswer: His spirit
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:1 states, 'I have put my spirit upon him,' showing divine empowerment.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 42:6 says the LORD will give his servant as a light to the Gentiles.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:6 says the LORD will 'give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles.'

questions.question: What does Isaiah 42:7 say the servant will do?
options: Open the blind eyes and bring out prisoners from prison
Destroy the nations
Build a temple in Jerusalem
Lead armies into battle
questions.correctAnswer: Open the blind eyes and bring out prisoners from prison
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:7 states the servant is to 'open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison.'

questions.question: What does the LORD say about His glory in Isaiah 42:8?
options: He will not give it to another
He will share it with angels
He will give it to kings
He will hide it forever
questions.correctAnswer: He will not give it to another
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:8 states, 'my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images.'

questions.question: What does Isaiah 42:9 say the LORD declares?
options: New things before they spring forth
Only the past events
Only the laws of Moses
The names of kings
questions.correctAnswer: New things before they spring forth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:9 says, 'new things do I declare: before they spring forth I tell you of them.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 42:10, who is called to sing a new song unto the LORD?
options: Ye that go down to the sea and all that is therein
Only the priests
Only the children of Israel
The kings of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Ye that go down to the sea and all that is therein
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:10 calls 'ye that go down to the sea, and all that is therein' to sing unto the LORD a new song.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 42:11 invites the inhabitants of the rock to shout from the mountains.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:11 says, 'let the inhabitants of the rock sing, let them shout from the top of the mountains.'

questions.question: Which action is described first in Isaiah 42:13?
options: The LORD shall go forth as a mighty man
The LORD will build a temple
The servant will cry softly
The mountains will be made waste
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD shall go forth as a mighty man
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:13 begins with 'The LORD shall go forth as a mighty man.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 42:8 says the LORD will give His praise to graven images.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:8 explicitly says the LORD will not give His praise to graven images.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 42:9 states that the LORD foretells new things before they happen.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:9 says the LORD declares new things before they spring forth.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 42 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 42 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 42:10, who is called to sing a new song and praise the LORD?
options: Those at the ends of the earth, including the sea and its inhabitants
Only the people of Israel
The priests and Levites in the temple
The kings and rulers of nations
questions.correctAnswer: Those at the ends of the earth, including the sea and its inhabitants
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:10 calls 'ye that go down to the sea, and all that is therein; the isles, and the inhabitants thereof' to sing unto the LORD a new song and praise Him, indicating a universal call to worship. This is further supported by Isaiah 42:11-12, which extends the call to wilderness, cities, and islands.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 42:11 describe the response of the wilderness and the villages of Kedar to God's praise?
options: They should lift up their voice and shout from the mountains
They should remain silent and meditate
They should gather for sacrifice
They should send offerings to the temple
questions.correctAnswer: They should lift up their voice and shout from the mountains
questions.explanation: Verse 11 commands the wilderness and the villages of Kedar to lift up their voice, and the inhabitants of the rock to sing and shout from the top of the mountains, demonstrating active praise. This complements verse 10’s call to worship and verse 12’s exhortation to glorify the LORD.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the praise and glory given according to Isaiah 42:12?
options: To give glory unto the LORD and declare His praise in the islands
To honor the kings and rulers
To seek forgiveness for sins
To celebrate harvest festivals
questions.correctAnswer: To give glory unto the LORD and declare His praise in the islands
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:12 explicitly states that the purpose is to give glory unto the LORD and declare His praise in the islands, emphasizing worship and recognition of God's majesty. This fits the theme of universal praise begun in verses 10 and 11.

questions.question: In Isaiah 42:13, how is the LORD described in His action against His enemies?
options: As a mighty man stirring up jealousy like a man of war who cries and prevails
As a gentle shepherd leading his flock
As a silent judge waiting patiently
As a healer who forgives all
questions.correctAnswer: As a mighty man stirring up jealousy like a man of war who cries and prevails
questions.explanation: Verse 13 portrays the LORD as a mighty warrior who stirs up jealousy, cries out, and prevails over enemies, showing His power and determination. This warrior imagery contrasts with His patient silence in verse 14 before acting decisively.

questions.question: What change in God's behavior is described in Isaiah 42:14 compared to before?
options: From holding peace and being still to crying out like a travailing woman and destroying swiftly
From being angry to becoming gentle and forgiving
From hiding Himself to revealing His glory gradually
From judging harshly to showing mercy
questions.correctAnswer: From holding peace and being still to crying out like a travailing woman and destroying swiftly
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:14 indicates God had been silent and refrained Himself for a long time, but now He will cry out like a travailing woman and act decisively to destroy and devour. This contrasts His previous patience with sudden action, as supported by verse 13’s warrior image.

questions.question: What natural elements does God say He will affect in Isaiah 42:15?
options: Mountains, hills, herbs, rivers, and pools
Trees, flowers, seas, and skies
Animals, birds, and fishes
Sun, moon, and stars
questions.correctAnswer: Mountains, hills, herbs, rivers, and pools
questions.explanation: Verse 15 states God will make waste of mountains and hills, dry up herbs, turn rivers into islands, and dry up pools, illustrating His control over creation and His power to bring judgment or change the natural order.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 42:16, how will God lead the blind?
options: By a way they knew not, in paths unknown, making darkness light and crooked things straight
By familiar roads and clear signs
Through the wilderness with a pillar of fire
By sending angels to guide them
questions.correctAnswer: By a way they knew not, in paths unknown, making darkness light and crooked things straight
questions.explanation: Verse 16 describes God leading the blind by unknown ways and making darkness light before them, symbolizing guidance in uncertainty and correction of what is crooked, showing His faithfulness not to forsake them.

questions.question: What consequence does Isaiah 42:17 say awaits those who trust in graven and molten images?
options: They shall be turned back and greatly ashamed
They shall be blessed and protected
They shall receive visions and dreams
They shall be rewarded with riches
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be turned back and greatly ashamed
questions.explanation: Verse 17 warns that those trusting in graven and molten images will be turned back and greatly ashamed, indicating God’s disapproval of idolatry and the resulting shame and failure.

questions.question: Based on Isaiah 42:18, what is the call to the deaf and blind?
options: Hear and look so that you may see
Remain silent and wait patiently
Pray without ceasing
Offer sacrifices to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Hear and look so that you may see
questions.explanation: Verse 18 calls the deaf to hear and the blind to look, with the purpose that they might see, symbolizing spiritual awakening and understanding.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 42:21 reveal about the LORD’s attitude toward His law and righteousness?
options: The LORD is well pleased for His righteousness' sake and will magnify and honor the law
The LORD is indifferent to the law
The LORD will abolish the old law and bring a new one
The LORD punishes those who follow the law
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is well pleased for His righteousness' sake and will magnify and honor the law
questions.explanation: Verse 21 states that the LORD is pleased for His righteousness and will magnify the law and make it honorable, highlighting God's commitment to justice and His law’s importance.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 42:22, what condition describes the people, and what is their situation?
options: They are robbed and spoiled, snared in holes, hid in prison houses, prey with no deliverer
They are free and prosperous, living in peace
They are honored and richly blessed by God
They are wandering but hopeful for future restoration
questions.correctAnswer: They are robbed and spoiled, snared in holes, hid in prison houses, prey with no deliverer
questions.explanation: Verse 22 portrays the people as robbed and spoiled, trapped in holes and prisons, prey without anyone to deliver or restore them, illustrating their desperate state due to disobedience (see verse 24).

questions.question: What does Isaiah 42:23 ask of the people in relation to the time to come?
options: Who will give ear and hearken to this message for the future?
Who will build temples and offer sacrifices?
Who will write new laws and decrees?
Who will gather armies for battle?
questions.correctAnswer: Who will give ear and hearken to this message for the future?
questions.explanation: Verse 23 questions who will listen and pay attention to the message for the time to come, emphasizing the importance of obedience and attentiveness to God's word.

questions.question: Who, according to Isaiah 42:24, gave Jacob and Israel into the hands of robbers and why?
options: The LORD gave them as spoil because of their sin and disobedience to His ways and law
Their enemies conquered them by might
They were betrayed by their own leaders
They chose to leave their land voluntarily
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD gave them as spoil because of their sin and disobedience to His ways and law
questions.explanation: Verse 24 clearly states that the LORD gave Jacob and Israel to robbers as punishment because they sinned and disobeyed His ways and laws, showing divine judgment for unfaithfulness.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 42:25 describe God's reaction to Israel's sinfulness despite their ignorance?
options: He poured out the fury of His anger and battle strength, setting them on fire, though they did not understand
He immediately forgave them and restored their fortunes
He sent prophets to warn them repeatedly without consequence
He abandoned them completely
questions.correctAnswer: He poured out the fury of His anger and battle strength, setting them on fire, though they did not understand
questions.explanation: Verse 25 depicts God’s fierce anger poured out on Israel, setting them on fire around but they did not perceive or take it to heart, illustrating the seriousness of their sins and their spiritual blindness.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 42:16 teaches that God will lead the blind in ways they already know.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:16 says God will bring the blind by a way they knew not and lead them in paths they have not known, showing His guidance is often through new and unexpected ways.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 42 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 42.

questions.question: Who is described as 'blind as the LORD's servant' in Isaiah 42:19?
options: The people of Israel
The prophet Isaiah
The LORD's servant
The kings of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD's servant
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:19 explicitly asks 'Who is blind, but my servant?' and answers that the LORD's servant is blind, indicating a paradoxical blindness related to the mission or perception of the servant.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 42:20 say about the servant's perception and hearing?
options: He sees clearly and hears well
He sees many things but does not observe; he opens ears but does not hear
He is deaf and blind
He observes all and listens attentively
questions.correctAnswer: He sees many things but does not observe; he opens ears but does not hear
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:20 states that the servant sees many things but does not observe, and opens ears but does not hear, indicating a spiritual or perceptual blindness and deafness despite physical senses.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 42:21, why is the LORD well pleased?
options: For His mighty works
For His righteousness' sake
For His mercy
For His patience
questions.correctAnswer: For His righteousness' sake
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:21 says the LORD is well pleased for His righteousness' sake, emphasizing the importance of righteousness in His actions and character.

questions.question: What is the condition of the people described in Isaiah 42:22?
options: They are victorious and free
They are robbed, spoiled, snared in holes, and hidden in prison houses
They are joyful and praising God
They are traveling to a new land
questions.correctAnswer: They are robbed, spoiled, snared in holes, and hidden in prison houses
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:22 describes the people as robbed and spoiled, snared in holes, and hidden in prison houses, indicating their captivity and suffering due to disobedience.

questions.question: Who is held responsible for giving Jacob for a spoil according to Isaiah 42:24?
options: The nations surrounding Israel
The LORD
The kings of Babylon
The servants of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:24 states that the LORD gave Jacob for a spoil and Israel to the robbers because of their sin and disobedience, showing divine judgment.

questions.question: What has the LORD poured upon Israel as a result of their sin, according to Isaiah 42:25?
options: Mercy and grace
The fury of His anger and the strength of battle
Peace and prosperity
Wisdom and understanding
questions.correctAnswer: The fury of His anger and the strength of battle
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:25 explains that the LORD poured out His anger and battle strength upon Israel as punishment for their disobedience.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage reflects the theme of spiritual blindness found in Isaiah 42:19-20?
options: Genesis 1:1-3
Psalm 23
Revelation 21:1-4
questions.explanation: John 9:39-41 discusses spiritual blindness and sight, echoing Isaiah 42:19-20’s themes of blindness and hearing, further developing the idea of recognizing true spiritual insight.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Isaiah 42:19-20 when contrasting seeing and not observing, or hearing and not understanding?
options: Metaphor
Chiasmus
Parallelism
Allegory
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:19-20 uses parallelism by pairing contrasts such as 'seeing many things but not observing' and 'opening ears but not hearing,' a common Hebrew poetic device to emphasize the paradox of spiritual blindness.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'magnify the law, and make it honourable' in Isaiah 42:21 suggest about the servant's mission?
options: To abolish the law
To increase the law’s importance and respect
To ignore the law
To rewrite the law
questions.correctAnswer: To increase the law’s importance and respect
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:21 indicates that the servant’s mission includes elevating the law’s status, making it more respected and honored among the people.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 42:23 challenge the audience in relation to the message?
options: It invites them to build altars
It asks who will listen and heed for the future
It commands silence
It tells them to leave the land
questions.correctAnswer: It asks who will listen and heed for the future
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:23 questions who among the audience will give ear and listen attentively to the prophetic message for what is to come.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 42:18 calls the deaf to hear and the blind to look so that they may see.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:18 explicitly states, 'Hear, ye deaf; and look, ye blind, that ye may see,' urging spiritual awakening.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 42:14 depicts the LORD as remaining silent and refraining from action forever.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:14 states that the LORD has been silent for a long time but now will cry out like a travailing woman and act decisively, so the statement is false.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated 'covenant' in Isaiah 42:6, and how does it relate to the servant's role?
options: Berith; a binding agreement symbolizing the servant as a mediator for the people
Chesed; lovingkindness
Ruach; spirit or breath
Shema; to hear or obey
questions.correctAnswer: Berith; a binding agreement symbolizing the servant as a mediator for the people
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 42:6, 'covenant' translates the Hebrew 'berith,' referring to a solemn binding agreement. The servant is given as a covenant to the people, indicating a mediatorial role between God and the nations.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the servant's mission to 'open the blind eyes' found in Isaiah 42:7?
options: Luke 4:18
Acts 2:38
Romans 8:28
Hebrews 11:1
questions.correctAnswer: Luke 4:18
questions.explanation: Luke 4:18 quotes Isaiah 61 and echoes Isaiah 42:7’s theme of opening blind eyes, emphasizing Jesus’ fulfillment of the servant’s role to bring sight to the spiritually blind.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 42:8 emphasize the uniqueness of the LORD in relation to idolatry?
options: By promising to create new gods
By declaring He will not share His glory or praise with graven images
By commanding the building of idols
By ignoring other gods
questions.correctAnswer: By declaring He will not share His glory or praise with graven images
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:8 states that the LORD will not give His glory or praise to another, especially not to graven images, emphasizing monotheism and rejection of idolatry.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 42 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 42 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 42:1, what is the role of God's servant upon whom He has put His spirit?
options: To bring forth judgment to the Gentiles
To conquer nations by force
To establish a political kingdom
To perform miraculous signs only
questions.correctAnswer: To bring forth judgment to the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:1 states that God’s servant, upon whom He has put His spirit, shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles, showing his role as a righteous judge and deliverer.

questions.question: What characteristic of the servant's voice is emphasized in Isaiah 42:2?
options: He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street
He shall shout loudly to gather the people
He shall sing praises in the temple
He shall roar like a lion in battle
questions.correctAnswer: He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:2 teaches that the servant will act with meekness and restraint, not using loud or disruptive cries in public places.

questions.question: Which doctrine is highlighted by the servant's treatment of the 'bruised reed' and 'smoking flax' in Isaiah 42:3?
options: Doctrine of mercy and gentleness
Doctrine of strict justice without compassion
Doctrine of sacrificial atonement alone
Doctrine of predestined election only
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of mercy and gentleness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:3 reveals the servant’s merciful nature, not breaking a bruised reed or quenching a smoking flax, symbolizing compassionate care for the weak and vulnerable.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily displayed in Isaiah 42:4 by the servant who 'shall not fail nor be discouraged'?
options: Perseverance and faithfulness
Omnipresence
Omniscience
Wrathful judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Perseverance and faithfulness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:4 shows the servant’s perseverance and faithfulness in carrying out God’s judgment until it is fully established on earth.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 42:5 reveal about God's creative power and providence?
options: God created the heavens and the earth and gives breath and spirit to all people
God is limited to only creating the earth
God's power is confined to Israel alone
God is a distant creator who does not sustain life
questions.correctAnswer: God created the heavens and the earth and gives breath and spirit to all people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:5 depicts God as the sovereign creator who not only made the heavens and earth but also gives life and spirit to all who walk upon the earth, affirming His providential care.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 42:6 express the servant's covenantal role for both Israel and the Gentiles?
options: The servant is called to be a covenant for the people and a light to the Gentiles
The servant is only a light to Israel and excludes Gentiles
The servant rejects covenant responsibilities
The servant is a symbol of political power
questions.correctAnswer: The servant is called to be a covenant for the people and a light to the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:6 shows the servant's role as mediator of God's covenant promises and light extending beyond Israel to the Gentiles, underscoring the universality of salvation.

questions.question: What is the servant’s mission described in Isaiah 42:7 regarding the blind and prisoners?
options: To open blind eyes and bring prisoners out of darkness
To imprison sinners without hope
To judge harshly without mercy
To maintain the status quo with no intervention
questions.correctAnswer: To open blind eyes and bring prisoners out of darkness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:7 emphasizes the servant’s mission to bring spiritual sight and freedom to those bound in darkness and captivity, revealing a redemptive and liberating role.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is prominently declared in Isaiah 42:8 when God says, 'my glory will I not give to another'?
options: God’s uniqueness and holiness
God’s impartiality
God’s omnipresence
God’s patience
questions.correctAnswer: God’s uniqueness and holiness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:8 reflects God’s unique holiness and sovereignty, affirming that His glory and praise belong exclusively to Him and not to idols or images.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 42:9 contribute to the doctrine of divine foreknowledge and revelation?
options: God declares new things before they happen
God only reveals the past
God reacts to events after they occur
God hides future events from His people
questions.correctAnswer: God declares new things before they happen
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:9 teaches that God declares future events before they spring forth, demonstrating His divine foreknowledge and sovereign revelation.

questions.question: What synthesis of Isaiah 42:10 and Isaiah 42:12 reveals about the global scope of worship?
options: All the earth, including seas, isles, and wilderness, is called to praise the LORD
Worship is limited to Jerusalem and Israel only
Only priests are authorized to worship God
Worship must be silent and private
questions.correctAnswer: All the earth, including seas, isles, and wilderness, is called to praise the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:10 and 42:12 together call for all creation—from the ends of the earth, seas, islands, wilderness, and villages—to lift up praise to God, emphasizing the universal call to worship.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 42:13 reveal about the LORD’s nature in relation to His enemies?
options: The LORD acts as a mighty warrior who prevails and stirs jealousy
The LORD is passive and avoids conflict
The LORD is indifferent to His enemies
The LORD only judges through human agents
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD acts as a mighty warrior who prevails and stirs jealousy
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:13 presents God as a mighty man of war who actively engages and prevails over His enemies, displaying His power and zeal.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the Bible’s promises of guidance are vague and unreliable. What does Isaiah 42:16 actually teach about God's guidance?
options: God will lead the blind by unknown ways, making darkness light and crooked things straight
God abandons those who are blind and confused
God only guides the righteous visibly
God's guidance is limited to Israel alone
questions.correctAnswer: God will lead the blind by unknown ways, making darkness light and crooked things straight
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:16 affirms that God actively guides those who are spiritually blind by paths they did not know, transforming darkness into light and crooked paths into straight ones, which refutes sceptical claims about unreliable guidance.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Isaiah 42:17 and Isaiah 42:19 give regarding spiritual blindness and servanthood?
options: Even God's servant can be blind and deaf, illustrating human spiritual weakness
Spiritual blindness is unrelated to God's people
Only Gentiles experience spiritual blindness
Spiritual sight is guaranteed for all servants of God
questions.correctAnswer: Even God's servant can be blind and deaf, illustrating human spiritual weakness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:17 and 42:19 together highlight that blindness and deafness are spiritual conditions affecting even those called servants of God, underscoring human frailty and need for divine restoration.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 42:21 teach about the LORD's pleasure in righteousness and the law?
options: The LORD is pleased with righteousness and will magnify and honor the law
The LORD rejects the law in favor of mercy only
The LORD is indifferent to human righteousness
The LORD’s law is obsolete
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is pleased with righteousness and will magnify and honor the law
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:21 shows God's pleasure in righteousness, promising to magnify the law and make it honorable, affirming the enduring value of God's moral standards.

questions.question: How do Isaiah 42:22 and Isaiah 42:24 together describe the consequences of Israel’s disobedience?
options: Israel is robbed, spoiled, and given to robbers due to sinning against the LORD
Israel remains untouched by sin and judgment
Israel is exalted for their obedience
Israel’s punishment is unjust and undeserved
questions.correctAnswer: Israel is robbed, spoiled, and given to robbers due to sinning against the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 42:22 and 42:24 describe how Israel suffers captivity and loss because of their sin and disobedience against God, illustrating the just consequences of covenant unfaithfulness.
